q-71578.name: Question 1
q-71578.problem: Which of the following describes the level surfaces of the function $f(x,y,z)=\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+{z}^{2})?$
q-71578.worked_solution:
The level surfaces of the function $f(x,y,z)$ are given by the following equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x,y,z) & =c \\ \operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+{z}^{2}) & =c \\ {x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+{z}^{2} & ={e}^{c}\end{aligned}
$$

If we let ${e}^{c}={r}^{2},$ we get

$$
{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+{z}^{2}={r}^{2}.
$$

Therefore, the level surfaces form a family of spheres centered at the origin.

a
A family of spheres centered at the origin

A family of surfaces given by z2+c=ln⁡(x2+y2)

A family of spheres centered at (0,0,e−c)

A family of spheres centered at (0,0,ec)
e
A family of surfaces given by z2+c=ex2+y2
Submit

The level surfaces of the function f(x,y,z) are given by the following equation:

f(x,y,z)=cln⁡(x2+y2+z2)=cx2+y2+z2=ec

x2+y2+z2=r2.

Therefore, the level surfaces form a family of spheres centered at the origin.

q-71580.problem: Which of the following describes the level surfaces of the function $f(x,y,z)=\frac{8}{x-2y+3z}?$
q-71580.worked_solution:
The level surfaces of the function $f(x,y,z)$ are given by the following equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x,y,z) & =c \\ \frac{8}{x-2y+3z} & =c \\ 8 & =c(x-2y+3z) \\ cx-2cy+3cz-8 & =0\end{aligned}
$$

Notice that $f(x,y,z)$ can't be zero. Therefore, we get a family of planes:

$$
cx-2cy+3cz-8=0,\,c\in (-\infty ,0)\cup (0,\infty ).
$$

Which of the following describes the c-level surfaces of the function f(x,y,z)=x2+y2−z2, where c>0?

a
A family of hyperboloids of one sheet: x2c2+y2c2−z2c2=1
b
A family of hyperboloids of one sheet: cx−2cy+3cz−8=0
c
A family of hyperbolic paraboloid: x2c2−y2c2=z
d
A family of spheres: x2c2+y2c2+z2c2=1
e
A family of ellipsoids: x2c2+y2c2+z2=1
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

The level surfaces of the function f(x,y,z) are given by the following equation:

f(x,y,z)=cx2+y2−z2=cx2+y2−z2=c2

Therefore, we get a family of hyperboloids of one sheet: x2c2+y2c2−z2c2=1,c∈(0,∞).

q-71596.problem: Find the equation of the level surface for the function $f(x,y,z)={x}^{2}+3(y-1)^{2}-{z}^{2}$ that passes through the point $P(4,2,1).$
q-71596.worked_solution:
First, we find the value of the function at $P$:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(4,2,1) & ={4}^{2}+3(2-1)^{2}-{1}^{2}=18\end{aligned}
$$

Recall that the level surfaces for the function $f(x,y,z)$ are given by the equation

$$
f(x,y,z)=c.
$$

In our case, we're interested in $c=18.$ So, we have:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x,y,z) & =c \\ {x}^{2}+3(y-1)^{2}-{z}^{2} & =18 \\ \frac{{x}^{2}}{18}+\frac{(y-1)^{2}}{6}-\frac{{z}^{2}}{18} & =1\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the level surface that passes through the point $P(4,2,1)$ is the hyperboloid of one sheet $\frac{{x}^{2}}{18}+\frac{(y-1)^{2}}{6}-\frac{{z}^{2}}{18}=1.$

q-129189.problem: Find the equation of the level surface for the function $f(x,y,z)={y}^{2}-{x}^{2}-z$ that passes through the point $P(0,-2,4).$
q-129189.worked_solution:
First, we find the value of the function at $P:$

$$
\begin{aligned}f(0,2,4) & ={2}^{2}-{0}^{2}-4 \\  & =4-0-4 \\  & =0\end{aligned}
$$

Recall that the level surfaces for the function $f(x,y,z)$ are given by the equation

$$
f(x,y,z)=c.
$$

In our case, we're interested in $c=0.$ So, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x,y,z) & =c \\ {y}^{2}-{x}^{2}-z & =0 \\ z & ={y}^{2}-{x}^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$
